issue.title: Spawn with controllers, extra tags, and minted roster team tags
issue.body:
## Background

FTS-6D of #2496, Phase 9, `critical path`, depends on #2551 (FTS-6C),
which must merge first. Its prerequisite chain supplies persisted faction
profiles, membership provenance, the relation authority, and owner-scoped
Lua operations. This issue adds profile requests at spawn ingress, the
local controller's roster team tag, and per-location occupant group tags.
Deliver the implementation, required documentation, and validation evidence
together in one PR.

Verified against `master` `293df10fb6e6` on 2026-09-10:

- `unit.spawn` accepts a legacy faction string in argument 4 or 5, with
  page and binding generation fixed at arguments 6 and 7
  (`src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/API/Units/Spawn.hs`). Portal spawns use
  `"player"`; the debug overlay uses `"debug"`.
- Both `spawnUnitContent` and `spawnEncounterUnitContent` in
  `scripts/locations.lua` independently default to `"hostile"`.
  `ruin_small` uses `count_range`, so its nomads take the dedicated
  encounter path. That path persists every successful roster prefix and
  retries only missing slots.
- Location instance integers start at 1 independently on each page.
  Durable location identity is `(WorldPageId, instance_id)`
  (`src/Location/Instance.hs`), not the integer alone.
- `Unit.Faction.Profile.relationFromTo` resolves live directed causes,
  then a shared non-null controller, then any shared tag, then base
  relations, then neutral. Tags have no separate culture/team precedence.
- Load reconciliation can legitimately change non-wire code in
  `World.Save.Types.fromUnitSnapshot` and `World.Load.Stage`.
  An empty diff under `src/World/Save` does not prove persistence safety.

Owner decisions:

- Only the engine's local controller may be requested in this slice,
  under one documented identity. Other controller requests fall back
  inertly as specified below.
- Nomads in different locations remain allied through their shared
  `nomad` tag. Applicable live relations retain their existing precedence;
  a hostile base-table entry alone does not override shared-tag alliance.
- Explicit location `player` and `debug` overrides retain their legacy
  control/capability behavior, with the location group tag added afterward
  and participating normally in relations.

## Requirements

1. **Profile ingress and compatibility.** `unit.spawn` accepts a profile
   request in either supported faction argument position, naming an
   optional local controller and optional extra tags with ownership.
   Start from the definition's FTS-3 default profile and add the requested
   controller/memberships. Document the exact table shape, owner fields,
   local-controller identity, and return behavior. Preserve legacy string
   mappings and fallbacks, including omitted faction, exactly as specified
   by #2515 and its canonical amendments; do not promise a universal
   inverse through the legacy `unit.getFaction` adapter.

   Preserve numeric Z, omitted Z, explicit nil Z, faction-slot precedence,
   and fixed page/binding argument positions. A stale or malformed binding
   remains a refusal before ID allocation or command queueing, returning
   `(nil, "page binding stale")`. Preserve the existing atomic page
   lifecycle admission and ordinary unbound failure convention. A refused
   portal spawn consumes no roster entry or supplies and issues no walk.

2. **Atomic request validation.** Validate profile fields by Lua type and
   validate the entire extra-tag collection before applying any requested
   field. Unknown controllers, malformed tags, wrong-typed owners, and
   malformed profile fields apply no requested controller or extra tags:
   for an otherwise admissible spawn, create the unit with its definition's
   FTS-3 defaults and emit exactly one refusal diagnostic for that request.
   Mixed valid/invalid requests have the same fallback, without partial
   ownership or membership changes and without a script exception. This
   fallback never bypasses a page/binding refusal. Syntactically valid
   minted tags remain accepted under the authoritative tag validator.

3. **Canonical roster membership.** Every locally controlled unit receives
   the same canonical roster team tag, deterministically derived from the
   complete local-controller identity and owned by spawn ingress. This
   covers profile requests, legacy `"player"` calls, portal spawns, and
   explicit `player` location overrides. Ordinary runtime owners cannot
   remove the ingress-owned membership. Overlapping membership under
   another owner retains that owner's provenance and removal semantics.

   During load reconciliation, add any missing canonical ingress-owned
   membership to saved local-controller units. Preserve all existing tags,
   owners, controller, and capabilities, including a same-tag membership
   held by another owner. Backfill is idempotent, logs once per actually
   backfilled unit, emits no backfill warning for an already-correct unit,
   and never fails a load solely because the membership was absent.

4. **Location composition through both paths.** For placed locations,
   update both `spawnUnitContent` and `spawnEncounterUnitContent`. With no
   explicit faction override, use the definition's FTS-3 default profile
   without a controller. With an explicit legacy string, use its complete
   D-26 mapping before adding the occupant group membership:

   - `player` retains local ownership, commandability, and canonical
     roster membership.
   - `debug` retains local commandability and unrestricted-combat
     capabilities without player ownership or roster membership.
   - Other legacy values retain their specified base-profile mapping.

   Add one shared occupant group tag under the location's owner identity
   regardless of the override. Consequently, even a legacy `neutral` or
   `debug` location unit can share group-based alliance; its capabilities
   and ownership remain governed separately. Do not introduce a special
   relation-precedence exception for these overrides.

   Derive both the tag and its owner deterministically and collision-free
   from the full `(WorldPageId, instance_id)` pair. Every occupant of one
   instance shares that group; distinct instances, including equal
   integers on different pages, have distinct tags and owners. Use the
   stored instance identity, not a newly allocated or inferred identity.

   Preserve registered encounter prefixes, exact existing unit IDs and
   homes, missing-slot-only retries, authored `contents` ordering, and
   one-time content/encounter lifecycle behavior. Hand-stamped locations
   without a placed instance retain their existing no-encounter behavior.
   Remove only `faction: hostile` from the shipped `ruin_small` unit entry;
   its nomads then carry authored `nomad` identity plus the occupant tag.

5. **Relations and control remain separate.** With no overriding live
   cause or shared controller/group, shipped nomad occupants are hostile
   to acolytes through the base table and neutral to wildlife. Occupants
   sharing a location group are allied even when their authored
   affiliations differ. Nomads from different locations are also allied
   through `nomad`, while retaining distinct occupant tags for future
   D-37 report scopes. Preserve live-cause precedence and directionality;
   this issue changes no relation consumer or policy.

   The debug overlay continues to pass `"debug"`. Preserve ownership,
   commandability, and discovery behavior under the selected mappings;
   alliance alone grants none of those properties. Demonstrate the same
   definition as an uncontrolled location occupant and a local-roster
   unit: identical authored identity, different controller and group
   memberships, and the corresponding authoritative policy answers.
   In particular, absent a live override, a locally controlled nomad is
   allied to its controller's acolyte roster while an uncontrolled nomad
   with no shared group is hostile to that roster.

6. **Persistence and documentation.** Preserve roster and occupant tag
   identities and every membership owner through the FTS-3 wire. Do not
   change serialized shapes, component versions, or retained codecs.
   Non-wire restore/reconciliation changes are allowed. Do not reseed
   saved authored identity from current definition defaults; roster
   backfill is the bounded reconciliation described above.

   Document the profile request and refusal behavior, location YAML
   `faction` semantics, and deterministic group/owner identities at their
   owning boundaries. Update `scripts/CLAUDE.md` and the applicable
   persistence inventory/contract notes. Required documentation and
   behavioral evidence are completion criteria of this implementation PR
   before final review and merge.

## Acceptance

Add a headless spec with top-level describe exactly `Faction spawn ingress`.
Exercise real Lua ingress and the production profile/relation authority:

- All legacy mappings and omission; profile requests in both faction
  positions; numeric/omitted/nil Z with explicit page and binding;
  stale/malformed bindings and page-change races without allocation,
  queueing, or portal side effects.
- Local-controller and tag-only requests; each invalid request class;
  a valid controller/tag followed by an invalid collection entry proving
  atomic fallback and exactly one diagnostic.
- Roster membership from portal, legacy `player`, and profile spawns;
  refusal of ordinary-owner removal; overlapping owners; missing-member
  restoration, preservation of all existing provenance, and a second
  reconciliation with no additional membership or backfill diagnostic.
- Both location paths, including ranged encounter content and interrupted
  prefix retry. Cover default and explicit `player`/`debug` mappings,
  shared membership within an instance, and distinct tag/owner identities
  for same-page instances and equal instance integers on different pages.
- The relation outcomes in requirement 5, including differing authored
  affiliations sharing only their occupant group, cross-location nomad
  alliance, and a directed live hostile cause overriding shared-tag
  alliance. Preserve the unaffected reverse answer. Use actual profiles,
  catalogue, and authority; populating the encounter fixture's stubbed
  `faction.relation` table is not evidence of these policy outcomes.
- Real-codec restore-and-recapture coverage for both minted tag kinds and
  all owners, including equal location integers on different pages, plus
  the load-backfill cases above. Retain prerequisite wire compatibility.

Extend the existing runtime probe coverage below to prove fresh-process
save/load/save preservation of those minted identities and provenance,
and successful, idempotent local-roster backfill from a fixture missing
the canonical membership. Poll load completion and reject unsuccessful
terminal outcomes. Keep codec tests and runtime persistence evidence
distinct; headless Hspec alone cannot prove `engine.saveWorld` end to end.

```bash
cabal build all
cabal build synarchy-test-headless
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Faction spawn ingress"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Unit faction profile policy"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Portal spawn page binding"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "persistent ruin encounter AI"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Unit faction profile wire"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Lua faction profile API"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Location instance identity"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Location discovery"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "persistence contract"'
python3 tools/test_lua_registration_audit.py
python3 tools/lua_registration_audit.py
python3 tools/lua_strict_decode_audit.py
python3 tools/test_location_content_probe.py
python3 tools/unicode_operator_audit.py
python3 tools/persistence_inventory_audit.py
python3 tools/enum_append_only_audit.py
python3 tools/run_probes.py --only location_content_probe
python3 tools/run_probes.py --only portal_location_probe
python3 tools/run_probes.py --only expedition_loop_probe
python3 tools/run_probes.py --only persistence_contract_probe
```

Expected: both builds succeed; every named spec group is non-empty and
passes; audits and the probe self-test exit zero; the four probes pass
sequentially. Run any additional subsystem guards selected by the actual
changed inputs. Include behavioral persistence results and a review of
serialized shapes, component versions, and retained codecs confirming
they are unchanged. An empty directory diff is neither required nor
sufficient evidence.

## Out of scope

- Other controllers or controller-change operations.
- Attack, Hold, escalation locking (FTS-6E), report delivery/reverse
  relations (FTS-6A), and diplomacy resolution (FTS-6F).
- Changes to relation precedence or forced cross-location neutrality.
- Removing legacy string forms, `unit.getFaction`, or the adapter (FTS-7).
- Encounter respawning, new nomad AI, or other authored location-content
  changes beyond removing the specified `faction` field.

## Related

- Epic #2496: FTS-6D, Phase 9, critical path. Blocked by #2551;
  #2515 and #2548 are earlier prerequisites.
- #916 (ruin encounters), #911 (location identity), #1686 (portal page
  binding), #2476 (page lifecycle admission), #2307 (load reconciliation).
- Supporting design: `docs/faction_tag_system_design.md`, D-1, D-5,
  D-10, D-22, D-26, D-29, D-34, D-37, and
  `docs/nomad_primitive_encounter_design.md`.

## Automated cross-agent issue review

Reviewed against `master@c3a4cd1331ba` by GPT-6-Astra (`gpt-6-astra` at `high`).

**Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED**

Corrections and spec additions below amend the implementation spec. Supporting context is non-normative. Open decisions remain unresolved and must not be guessed.

### Corrections
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Qualify occupant tag and owner identities by (WorldPageId, instance_id), using a deterministic, collision-free representation. LocationInstanceId is allocated independently on each page, starting at 1; deriving identity from the integer alone merges unrelated groups (src/Location/Instance.hs:21–25; WorldQuery/Location.hs:171).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Update the production integration surface to include spawnEncounterUnitContent as well as spawnUnitContent. The shipped ruin_small uses count_range and therefore follows the dedicated encounter path, which independently defaults to "hostile". Preserve its registered-prefix retry behavior and the authored contents ordering (scripts/locations.lua:495, :745; data/locations/ruin_small.yaml:108–133).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Replace the blanket empty diff requirement for src/World/Save with verification that serialized shapes, component versions, and retained codecs remain unchanged. Non-wire restoration changes are legitimate: the cited reconciliation precedent lives in src/World/Save/Types.hs:876 and is consumed by src/World/Load/Stage.hs:1068.

### Spec additions / clarifications
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Exercise profile requests in both supported faction argument positions, including explicit nil Z and page/binding arguments. Preserve stale-binding refusal before allocation or queueing, and verify a mixed valid/invalid profile request applies no partial controller or extra-tag changes and logs once (src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/API/Units/Spawn.hs:70–97; requirement 1).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Test that legacy "player" spawns also receive the canonical roster membership; ordinary runtime owners cannot remove that membership; and load backfill is idempotent, preserves existing tags and owners, and emits no backfill warning for an already-correct unit (requirements 2 and 7; design D-22 and D-34).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Add save/load coverage proving both minted tag identities and their provenance survive restoration, including equal instance integers on different pages. Use behavioral restoration evidence rather than treating the unchanged wire diff as persistence proof (requirement 7; src/World/Save/CLAUDE.md, Gates).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Prove relation outcomes through the real faction authority. The existing ruin encounter fixture supplies relation answers through a Lua stub, so merely adding expected entries to that stub cannot validate the catalogue or profile composition. Include a shared occupant-tag case with differing authored affiliations to establish that the group tag itself supplies alliance (test-headless/Test/Headless/Lua/UnitAiEncounter.hs:57; Unit/Faction/Profile.hs:435).

### Supporting context
- **GPT-6-Astra:** The checked-out SHA matches c3a4cd1331baa2f9910f3e3844f8f7ff1e58b65a. Its spawn ingress remains scalar; the missing later profile integration was evaluated under the declared-prerequisite assumption, not treated as a blocker (src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/API/Units/Spawn.hs; dossier dependency chain).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Shared membership unconditionally supplies alliance below live causes and above base relations. This is implemented by relationFromTo and explicitly tested; tags have no separate culture/team precedence (src/Unit/Faction/Profile.hs:435–453; test-headless/Test/Headless/Unit/FactionProfile.hs:335–344; design, Directed relation precedence).

### Open decisions
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Should different locations' nomads remain allied through their shared "nomad" tag, or is cross-location neutrality an intentional policy change? Requirement 4 demands neutrality while requiring unchanged authority and preserved authored tags; those conditions cannot all hold under relationFromTo (src/Unit/Faction/Profile.hs:435–453; design D-29).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** For an explicit location faction override of "player" or "debug", does full D-26 compatibility apply, or does location spawning intentionally retain only affiliation and force no controller/capabilities? Requirement 3's unconditional no-controller wording conflicts with D-26's player mapping and requirement 5's unchanged ownership/commandability promise; the current location paths forward the supplied string unchanged (scripts/locations.lua:451, :497; design D-26).

### Recommended disposition
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Revise requirement 4 to preserve cross-location nomad alliance unless the owner explicitly chooses a separately specified policy change; distinct occupant tags still provide distinct report scopes under D-37. Resolve the explicit location-override semantics, incorporate the bounded amendments above, and rerun readiness review.

### Reviewer summaries
- **GPT-6-Astra — CHANGES REQUESTED:** The ingress work is justified, but requirement 4 contradicts the established shared-tag alliance policy. Explicit legacy location overrides also need a consistent ownership contract. The remaining integration and acceptance gaps can be resolved through amendments.

## Automated cross-agent issue rereview

Reviewed against `master@293df10fb6e6` by Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1` at `high`).

**Verdict: APPROVE**

Corrections and spec additions below amend the implementation spec. Supporting context is non-normative. Open decisions remain unresolved and must not be guessed.

### Corrections
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Acceptance command list: the describe groups `Unit faction profile wire` and `Lua faction profile API` do not exist at master 293df10fb (grep of test-headless/ finds neither; only `Unit faction profile policy` at test-headless/Test/Headless/Unit/FactionProfile.hs:127). They are expected from prerequisites #2515 and #2551. If those PRs landed the groups under different top-level names, run the actual prerequisite group names instead; the requirement is that the prerequisite wire and Lua-API suites stay green, not the literal strings.

### Spec additions / clarifications
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Hand-stamped location content with no placed instance (the `placed == nil` branch in scripts/locations.lua:728, :749, :575) receives NO occupant group tag and no location owner: there is no stored `(WorldPageId, instance_id)` to derive from, and the negative `lootInstanceId` at scripts/locations.lua:715-718 is an inferred loot key, never an identity. Such units take only the definition default profile (or the explicit legacy mapping). This follows from requirement 4's 'stored instance identity, never inferred' rule and must be covered by one acceptance case.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Deterministic, collision-free derivation of the roster tag, the occupant tag, and the location owner must be an injective encoding over the full input, not a hash. The tag validator admits any non-empty whitespace-free text (src/Unit/Faction/Profile.hs:223-224) and `WorldPageId` is arbitrary Lua-supplied text (src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/API/Units/Spawn.hs:182), which may contain whitespace or the separator, so the encoding must escape or length-prefix the page id component. Acceptance should include a page id containing a separator-like character and whitespace, proving distinct tags/owners and a valid tag.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** The ingress owner identity (roster tag) and each derived location owner identity must be distinct from every owner an ordinary Lua caller can claim through #2551's owner-scoped add/remove operations, so that requirement 3's 'ordinary runtime owners cannot remove the ingress-owned membership' cannot be bypassed by a script passing the ingress owner's name. Document that reservation at the owning boundary and cover it with one acceptance case attempting removal under a spoofed owner string. Both identities must also be representable in the prerequisite's persisted owner provenance without a codec or component-version change (requirement 6); if they are not, stop and escalate rather than bumping a version in this PR.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Requirement 5 relies on the encounter consumer already reading relations through the unit-id authority. At master 293df10fb, scripts/unit_ai_encounter.lua:80 still resolves hostility as `faction.relation(unit.getFaction(uid), unit.getFaction(target)) == "hostile"`; under D-31's adapter a nomad profile carrying `nomad` plus an occupant tag is not one of the five exact legacy profiles and would read as `neutral`, so nomads would never engage. FTS-5 (#2521, D-33) is assumed to have ported that caller. The PR must demonstrate, via `location_content_probe` and the `persistent ruin encounter AI` group against the real ingress, that shipped nomad occupants still engage acolytes after `faction: hostile` is removed. If any shipped consumer on that path still goes through the string adapter, report it as a prerequisite gap rather than silently porting a consumer under this issue's 'changes no relation consumer' constraint.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Location YAML `faction` is parsed as an optional untyped string (src/Engine/Asset/YamlLocations.hs:89) with no vocabulary check; requirement 4's documentation must state that an unrecognized value follows the same warn-once inert fallback as `unit.spawn` (Spawn.hs:217-231 today) and still receives the occupant group tag, and one acceptance case must cover an unknown location `faction` string.

### Supporting context
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Checked-out snapshot is 293df10fb6e6 (dossier base_sha; HEAD in the worktree). `uiFactionId ∷ !Faction` is still scalar (src/Unit/Types/Instance.hs:102) and Unit.Faction.Profile's header says nothing in it is live, so FTS-2/3/6B/6C (#2506, #2515, #2548, #2551) are absent here and were evaluated as assumed contracts per the dependency policy; the design ledger lists them as filed (docs/faction_tag_system_design.md:20-26).
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Prior review's two open decisions are resolved in the body: 'Nomads in different locations remain allied through their shared `nomad` tag' and 'Explicit location `player` and `debug` overrides retain their legacy control/capability behavior, with the location group tag added afterward' (Owner decisions; requirements 4 and 5). Both agree with `relationFromTo` (src/Unit/Faction/Profile.hs:435-453) and with `legacyPlayerProfile`/`legacyDebugProfile` (Profile.hs:506-525).
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Spawn ingress claims verified: slot-4 type discrimination, slot-5 precedence, slot 6 page, slot 7 binding, and `boundSpawnStale` refusing before `nextUnitId` and before the queue write (src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/API/Units/Spawn.hs:113-132, :185-187, :234, :251). Portal spawn passes "player" with page and bindGen and abandons the tick on the stale refusal (scripts/building_spawn.lua:227-241); the debug overlay passes "debug" (scripts/init_mouse.lua:212-213).
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Both location paths independently default to "hostile" (scripts/locations.lua:451, :497); ruin_small's nomad entry uses `count_range` with `faction: hostile` (data/locations/ruin_small.yaml:123-124), so it takes `spawnEncounterUnitContent`, which persists every successful prefix and resumes at the next missing slot (locations.lua:501-535). Instance ids are per-page from 1 (src/Location/Instance.hs:21-25, :149-150) and Lua rows carry `instance_id` alongside the page (src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/API/WorldQuery/Location.hs:88, :171).
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Load-reconciliation precedent for non-wire changes exists at src/World/Save/Types.hs:876 (`fromUnitSnapshot`) consumed by src/World/Load/Stage.hs:1068, supporting requirement 6's allowance.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** All listed tools exist under tools/ and all four probes are registered in tools/probe_runner_registry.py (lines 106, 134, 171, 192); none is marked needs-GPU. Existing describe groups resolve: `Portal spawn page binding (#1686)`, `persistent ruin encounter AI (#916)`, `Location instance identity`, `Location discovery`, `Unit faction profile policy`, `persistence contract`. The encounter fixture's `faction.relation` is a Lua stub (test-headless/Test/Headless/Lua/UnitAiEncounter.hs:57-58), confirming the acceptance note that populating it is not policy evidence.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** D-28 base table makes acolyte/nomad hostile and nomad/wildlife undeclared (neutral) (docs/faction_tag_system_design.md:866-872), matching requirement 5. D-34 and D-37 (design lines 919-932, 956-967) specify ingress-owned roster tags with load backfill and per-location occupant tags under the location's ownership, matching requirements 3 and 4.

### Reviewer summaries
- **Claude Fable 5.1 — APPROVE:** The revision resolves both prior open decisions (cross-location nomad alliance through the shared `nomad` tag is now an explicit owner decision; explicit `player`/`debug` location overrides keep their full D-26 mapping with the occupant tag added afterward) and incorporates every prior correction: `(WorldPageId, instance_id)` qualification, both `spawnUnitContent` and `spawnEncounterUnitContent`, and the empty-diff requirement replaced by a shape/version/codec review plus behavioral persistence evidence. Independently checked against master 293df10fb: the Spawn.hs argument layout, `boundSpawnStale` refusal ordering, both locations.lua paths defaulting to "hostile", ruin_small's `count_range` entry with `faction: hostile`, per-page instance-id allocation, and `relationFromTo` precedence all match the body. Every named tool, probe, and existing describe group resolves in the snapshot; the two groups not present ("Unit faction profile wire", "Lua faction profile API") belong to declared prerequisites. Remaining gaps are clarifications my amendments can settle: hand-stamped content with no placed instance, injective encoding of the minted identities under the permissive tag validator, non-claimability of the two ingress owner identities, and a prerequisite-consumer check on the encounter path.
